questions.q: Why can General Ledger allow a company to staff journal entry and journal posting with different people, even though both happen on the same Journals page?
options: They are controlled by the same single privilege
Posting is not actually a secured action
Journal entry can only ever be performed by a manager
They are secured by separate function security privileges underneath one page
questions.explain: Creating a journal entry and posting it are commonly controlled by different privileges, allowing a company to require different roles for each action even on the same page.

questions.q: What is the primary data security dimension that scopes a General Ledger accountant's ability to post?
options: Business unit
Data access set (ledger and balancing segment values)
Asset book
Control budget
questions.explain: General Ledger posting is scoped by the accountant's data access set, which governs which ledgers and balancing segment values they can act on.

questions.q: In Payables, which step is commonly gated by an approval-limit rule tied to invoice amount?
options: Invoice entry
Invoice validation/matching to a purchase order
Invoice approval
Business unit assignment
questions.explain: Invoice approval is commonly subject to an approval-limit rule based on the dollar amount of the invoice, separate from entry and matching.

questions.q: At Castellan Robotics, why does writing off an Accounts Receivable balance over a defined threshold require an AR Manager rather than an AR Specialist?
options: A write-off directly affects reported revenue, so it is a deliberate design choice to hold that privilege at the manager level
It is a technical limitation of the Receivables module that cannot be changed
AR Specialists are not allowed to use the Receivables module at all
Write-offs require a different ledger entirely
questions.explain: Write-offs are typically held more tightly than routine adjustments because they directly affect reported revenue — a deliberate design choice reflected in which duty roles the AR Manager job role inherits.

questions.q: What is the general pattern that repeats across GL, AP, and AR security?
options: Every action is available to every job role equally
Only managers can ever use any of the three modules
Routine entry work sits in specialist-level duty roles, higher-risk/irreversible actions sit in manager-level duty roles, and data security scopes all of it
Data security only applies to General Ledger, never to AP or AR
questions.explain: All three modules separate routine, specialist-level entry work from higher-risk, manager-level actions (posting, approval, write-off), with data security scoping access throughout.
